title: Cap. X Arg. X Major: God knows infinite modes to turn any heart; to deny this denies omnipotence — Prov. xxi. 1; Augustine De corr. et grat. 14
pass_a_gloss: That first I take; that God knows infinite modes by which he can bend the heart of any man unto freely repenting, believing, and persevering. Who denies this denies God’s omnipotence, denies God’s absolute dominion over human wills, against that of Solomon, The king’s heart is in the hand of the Lord; whithersoever he will he has inclined it, Prov. xxi. 1. Unto which Augustine subscribes, De corrept. et gratia, cap. 14. Of the very wills of men he does what he wills, and when he wills, having the most omnipotent power of inclining human hearts whithersoever he wills.
pass_b_english: First I take this: God knows infinite ways to bend any man’s heart to repent, believe, and persevere freely. Who denies it denies God’s omnipotence and his absolute lordship over human wills—against Solomon (Prov. xxi. 1): The king’s heart is in the Lord’s hand; he turns it wherever he wills. Augustine subscribes (De correptione et gratia 14): Of men’s very wills he does what he wills, when he wills, holding most omnipotent power to incline human hearts wherever he wills.
source_text: Illud imprimis sumo; Deum nosse infinitos modos quibus cor cujuscunque hominis flectere possit ad libere poenitendum, credendum, et perseverandum. Qui hoc negat, negat Dei omnipotentiam, negat Dei supra voluntates humanas absolutum dominium, contra illud Solomonis, Cor regis in manu Domini; quocunque voluerit inclinavit illud, Prov. xxi. 1. Cui subscribit Augustinus, De corrept. et gratia, cap. 14. De ipsis hominum voluntatibus facit quod vult, et quando vult, habens humanorum cordium quo vult inclinandorum omnipotentissimam potestatem.
